questions.question: In eutectic high entropy alloys, does the HPHT-induced coherent interface mechanism fail to arrest interfacial cracking if the pressure exceeds the threshold required to maintain phase stability, and what specific strain-hardening rate measurement distinguishes this failure from the observed homogeneous deformation?
questions.rationale: Answering this changes the process window selection for HPHT treatment; if the mechanism fails at higher pressures, the optimal operating regime must be narrowed to preserve the strength-ductility synergy.
questions.decision_use: To define the maximum allowable pressure limit for the HPHT treatment to ensure interface coherence and prevent catastrophic failure modes like interfacial cracking.
answer_requirements: Quantitative measurement of strain-hardening rate and interfacial crack density at incremental pressure steps (e.g., 5, 10, 15 GPa) to identify the threshold where GND density homogenization ceases.
evidence_spans: Dislocations preferentially initiate in the softer FCC phase, and subsequently are allowed to transfer into the harder B2 phase due to the highly coherent interface, which effectively alleviates stress concentration at the interface and coordinates deformation between the two phases.

Upon further loading, the GND density of the B2 phase increases much faster than that of the FCC phase, eventually resulting in an identical value of GND density in both phases at 35% strain, consistent with a homogeneous plastic deformation distribution (Fig. 3c ).

questions.question: In the HPHT-treated CoCrFeNiCu eutectic high entropy alloy, does the homogeneous deformation mechanism (GND density matching between B2 and FCC phases) hold at strain levels exceeding 35%, and does the work-hardening capability degrade if the strain exceeds the uniform elongation limit where the GND densities converge?
questions.rationale: Answering this defines the safe operating strain limit for structural applications; if the mechanism breaks down post-convergence, the design must incorporate a safety factor or fail-safe architecture.
questions.decision_use: To set the maximum allowable design strain for components made from this HPHT-treated alloy to avoid premature failure due to loss of work-hardening capacity.
answer_requirements: In-situ EBSD measurement of GND density evolution and local fracture surface analysis at strain levels >35% to determine if the GND matching persists or if localized shear bands form.
evidence_spans: Upon further loading, the GND density of the B2 phase increases much faster than that of the FCC phase, eventually resulting in an identical value of GND density in both phases at 35% strain, consistent with a homogeneous plastic deformation distribution (Fig. 3c ).
In comparison with the Ac, Ac+HPHT and Ho alloys, the work-hardening capability of HPHT-treated alloy is much more pronounced and stable up to the tensile plastic instability region.
